_transfer_overrides_note: Global defaults applied to every Fusion FA bookTransfer / transferAsset call.  Per-row TARGET_LOCATION_ID / TARGET_EXPENSE_CCID from BIP still win.  Note: do NOT set conversion_rate_type globally — it is ledger-specific.  When unset the parameter is omitted, which is required for same-currency transfers and for ledgers that don't publish that rate type.  Other recognised keys: book_transfer_type_code (default 'NBV'), cost_basis_code (default 'COST_RESERVE_SRC'), retirement_type_code (default 'TRF TO NEW BOOK' — the source-book retirement reason for cross-book transfers; set to '' to omit), copy_dff_flag, copy_asset_key_flag, create_new_asset_flag, use_dest_cat_deprn_rules_flag, use_xfr_date_as_dpis_flag.
_transfer_overrides_by_book_note: Per-book overrides, keyed by book code (case-insensitive).  Each entry may carry an 'applies_to' flag controlling when its values are layered onto the payload: 'T' (target, default) for inbound transfers into this book, 'S' (source) for outbound, 'B' for both.  Source overrides apply first; target overrides win when both supply the same key.  Books not listed transfer with no per-book values.
_post_transfer_attribute_update_note: Opt-in follow-up after a successful cross-book bookTransfer.  Resolves the destination asset_id in this order: (1) custom BIP report (dest_lookup_bip) - recommended; (2) X_NEW_ASSET_ID etc. on the bookTransfer response; (3) X_NEW_ASSET_NUMBER + getAssetInformation against target book; (4) fallback to source asset_number against target book.  Then calls processTransaction-updateAssetDescriptiveDetails with the bumped value.  Suffix rule: 'X' -> 'X_1', 'X_1' -> 'X_2', etc.  Default off.
_account_combination_service_note: Optional.  When the BIP report supplies destination segments via TARGET_SEG1..TARGET_SEGN columns (or the Option B same-book company-segment swap path can't find a matching code combination in the destination ledger), the runner first tries to look up an existing CCID via accountCombinationsLOV.  If no match, it falls through to the SOAP AccountCombinationService.validateAndCreateAccounts to mint one on demand.  Requires the GL_MANAGE_GENERAL_LEDGER_ACCOUNT_COMBINATIONS_PRIV privilege on the integration user.  Oracle still validates the combination against cross-validation rules, segment-value security, and date ranges — those failures come back as Status='E' with an Error message and the runner records the transfer as FAILED.  Omit this block (or set enabled=false) to skip auto-creation: the resolver will raise ValidationError listing the segments that need to be created manually in Oracle GL.  ``ledger_name_by_book`` maps each target book to the GL ledger that owns its chart of accounts.

account_combination_service._dynamic_insertion_note: Literal value Oracle wants in the <acc:DynamicInsertion> element.  Most pods accept 'Yes'; some require 'y' or 'true'.  Check your tenant's WSDL sample if in doubt.
account_combination_service._skip_lov_lookup_note: When true, skip the REST accountCombinationsLOV lookup and call SOAP validateAndCreateAccounts directly.  Oracle returns the existing CcId when the combination already exists (Status=S) or mints it when it doesn't.  Useful when accountCombinationsLOV is flaky on your pod (Citadel dev1).  Default false (preserves the lookup-first behaviour).
account_combination_service._optional_tail_fields_note: Schema-optional elements in the documented Oracle template (EnabledFlag, FromDate, ToDate).  Omit / leave null to keep them out of the envelope.  Set as strings when your pod requires them.
account_combination_service._segment_defaults_note: Per-segment filler for slots the BIP report does NOT populate.  List exactly the segments your chart of accounts has — this caps the SOAP envelope at your COA's segment count (no Segment14..30 noise) AND uses the correct width-specific filler per segment.  The report supplies the meaningful segments (1/2/3/5 etc.); these fill the rest.  Example below is a 13-segment Citadel COA: E00573973.6506300.30403.999999999999.1008.9999999999.999.999999999.9.9.9.9.9
account_combination_service._pad_segments_note: Crude fallback: fill EVERY still-missing slot up to pad_segments_to with one value.  Prefer segment_defaults above (per-segment, COA-accurate).  Leave pad_segments_to=0 when segment_defaults covers your COA.
account_combination_service._ledger_name_by_book_note: FALLBACK ONLY.  The GL ledger is sourced per-row from the BIP report's TARGET_LEDGER_NAME column.  This static book->ledger map is consulted only when that column is blank for a row.  Safe to leave empty when the report always supplies TARGET_LEDGER_NAME.

post_transfer_attribute_update._source_field_note: Lower-case AssetState field name OR DFF slot read from getAssetInformation.  DEFAULT 'tag_number' targets Oracle FA's canonical header Tag Number (X_TAG_NUMBER) — the field with FA uniqueness behaviour that feeds the FA asset reports.  bookTransfer does NOT copy this to the destination, so without the bump the new asset's header Tag Number is left blank.  Set to 'attribute10' / 'cat_attribute7' / etc. instead only if your tenant tracks the canonical tag in a DFF.  Mirror this in fusion_parameter below.
post_transfer_attribute_update._fusion_parameter_note: Matching P_<NAME> bind parameter for processTransaction-updateAssetDescriptiveDetails.  Must mirror source_field.  DEFAULT 'P_TAG_NUMBER' for the canonical header tag; use 'P_CAT_ATTRIBUTE7' for the CMDB tag DFF, 'P_ATTRIBUTE10' for standard FA DFF slot 10.
post_transfer_attribute_update._also_bump_params_note: Secondary fusion params that receive the SAME bumped value on both source-side and destination-side updates.  Typical use at Citadel: primary updates P_TAG_NUMBER (canonical FA header tag), also_bump_params=['P_CAT_ATTRIBUTE7'] mirrors the same _N value into the CMDB tag DFF so the two stay in lockstep (the asset header and the CMDB record never disagree on the active tag).
post_transfer_attribute_update._contract_note: Per-transfer behaviour: normally TWO updateAssetDescriptiveDetails POSTs land per cross-book transfer.  (1) The RETIRED SOURCE asset gets its tag suffixed with _<N> where N is its chain_order from dest_lookup_bip (1 for first transfer, 2 for second, etc.).  (2) The NEW DESTINATION asset gets the clean canonical tag (suffix stripped).  This frees the canonical tag for the new active asset while keeping each historical retired record uniquely identifiable.  Same-book transfers do NOT run this path — they keep their asset_id and tag unchanged.  When the SOURCE asset has no tag at all, the Tag Number bump is skipped (a previously-untagged asset is never seeded with _1) — the destination POST still applies its populate/clear DFF updates, and the source POST is sent only if source-side DFFs are configured.
post_transfer_attribute_update._clear_dest_dffs_note: Params to send with empty-string values on the DESTINATION update only, CLEARING directive DFFs that were only meaningful pre-transfer (Transfer to Entity / Transfer to Location).  NOTE: empty-string clears work for CHAR DFFs only — Oracle FA treats '' as 'no change' for DATE-typed DFFs, so a Transfer DATE field cannot be blanked this way.  Default it to the current date via populate_dest_dffs (${current_date}) instead — see P_CAT_ATTRIBUTE_DATE1 below.  Param names match Citadel's pre_bip_dff_updates.field_parameter_map.
post_transfer_attribute_update._clear_source_dffs_note: Symmetric to clear_dest_dffs but for the source asset (rare — most directive DFFs only matter on the destination side).
post_transfer_attribute_update._populate_dest_dffs_note: Params to set on the DESTINATION update with templated values — typically Source Asset Book / Source Asset Number DFFs so the new asset points back at its origin.  Values support placeholders: ${source_asset_id}, ${source_asset_number}, ${source_book_type_code}, ${target_book_type_code}, ${target_asset_id}, ${target_asset_number}, ${transfer_to_entity}, ${transfer_date}, ${current_date}, ${original_tag}, ${source_new_tag}, ${destination_new_tag}.  ${current_date} is today as YYYY-MM-DD.  Unknown placeholders are left in place so misconfig is visible in --debug dumps.  P_CAT_ATTRIBUTE2 = Source Asset Book; P_CAT_ATTRIBUTE3 = Source Asset Number; P_CAT_ATTRIBUTE_DATE1 = Transfer Date, defaulted to ${current_date} because Oracle FA won't blank a DATE DFF with an empty string (per the Asset Category DFF setup at Citadel).
post_transfer_attribute_update._populate_source_dffs_note: Symmetric to populate_dest_dffs but applied to the source-side update.  Rare.
post_transfer_attribute_update._dest_lookup_bip_note: Recommended: a custom BIP report that returns the lineage chain for a transferred asset.  Canonical SQL is in sql/get_transferred_asset.sql (recursive walk over a merged edge set: TRUE bookTransfer rows in FA_BOOK_TRANSFER_DISTS PLUS historical addition+retirement hops recovered from the 'Source Asset Number' DFF, so hand-migrated assets still chain correctly).  Serves two purposes: (a) pick the freshly-created destination (the row whose BOOK_TYPE_CODE matches the in-flight target book), and (b) provide the chain_order of the source link so we know what suffix number to apply (1 for first transfer, 2 for second, etc.).  When omitted, source suffix falls back to bump_underscore_suffix (less accurate — can't distinguish 'clean tag from prior cycle' from 'never been transferred').
